rules.statement: Every code path that sets a local account's password (management create/reset, self-service change, seeders) must validate it through the single shared password policy service before the password is hashed, rather than relying on a store's own validators such as ASP.NET Core Identity's password validators.
rules.why: Stores differ in what they refuse, Identity's defaults impose composition rules, and a custom store would skip them; one policy refuses a password in one place whichever path sets it, and a refused password is never hashed.
rules.check: Look for new or changed password-setting paths that hash or store a password without first calling the password policy, or that add per-store password validation rules.

rules.statement: Count password length in Unicode code points (runes, e.g. via `EnumerateRunes()`) over the whole password, never in UTF-16 `char`s, and never truncate the password.
rules.why: NIST SP 800-63B-4 counts each Unicode code point as one character, so a surrogate pair is one character, and the whole password must be judged.
rules.check: Flag password length checks using `.Length` on a string/span of chars, or code that truncates or substrings a password before validating, hashing or comparing.

rules.statement: Do not impose password composition rules (required digits, uppercase, symbols, character classes); enforce only length limits and blocklists.
rules.why: NIST SP 800-63B-4 forbids composition rules because they lead users to predictable substitutions.
rules.check: Flag password validation that requires character classes or sets options like RequireDigit/RequireUppercase/RequireNonAlphanumeric.

rules.statement: A password blocklist compares the whole password with each entry, ignoring case, and refuses passwords equal to the account's user name, email, or email local part.
rules.why: NIST requires comparing the whole password against commonly used, expected and compromised passwords; the account's own names are expected passwords.
rules.check: Look for blocklist checks that use substring/prefix matching, case-sensitive comparison, or omit the account-name check.

rules.statement: Do not call a network breached-password service by default; such a check must be an opt-in pluggable blocklist registered by the deployment.
rules.why: A default network call would make every password change depend on a third party's availability and require a privacy review.
rules.check: Flag default registrations or policy code that make HTTP calls (e.g. to Pwned Passwords) during password validation.

rules.statement: When a password policy refuses a password, report the specific reason (an error code plus a description naming the requirement, such as the minimum length) to the caller.
rules.why: NIST requires the verifier to give the reason when it refuses a password, and the UI maps the code to guidance.
rules.check: Flag password refusals that return a generic failure without an error code or a description of the requirement.

rules.statement: In a self-service password change, validate the new password against the policy before verifying the current password.
rules.why: The source requires the change to judge the new password first and report a policy refusal by its error code.
rules.check: In password change flows, check that the policy call comes before current-password verification.

rules.statement: Code that consumes an open vocabulary of error codes must handle unknown codes with a general fallback (for example a general message) instead of assuming the known set is exhaustive.
rules.why: Error-code vocabularies are open, so a replacement implementation may report other codes.
rules.check: Flag switches/maps over error codes that throw or fail on unrecognized values, or that have no default branch.

rules.statement: A result type whose error members are populated only on failure should annotate its status property with `[MemberNotNullWhen]` naming those members.
rules.why: The source defines its result classes with `IsRejected`/`IsChanged` annotated so callers get correct nullability flow for `Error`/`ErrorDescription`.
rules.check: Flag new result classes with nullable error properties and a boolean status property lacking `[MemberNotNullWhen]`.

rules.statement: Register implementations of a strategy collection (multiple implementations of one interface consumed as `IEnumerable<T>`) with `TryAddEnumerable`.
rules.why: The policy consumes all registered blocklists in registration order, and hosts must be able to add their own without duplicates.
rules.check: Flag strategy-collection registrations using `AddSingleton`/`TryAddSingleton` for an interface consumed as an enumerable.

rules.statement: Bundled third-party data files must be pinned to a specific source commit, reproducible by a script that verifies the source's SHA-256, and attributed with their license in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md shipped in the package.
rules.why: The source requires the embedded password list to be reproducible from a pinned, verified source with recorded attribution and licenses.
rules.check: Look for added embedded resources or data files derived from third-party sources without a pinned commit, a verifying update script, or a THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES entry.

rules.statement: Load a large embedded lookup resource once, lazily on first use, into a frozen collection (e.g. `FrozenSet<T>`) rather than reading it per call.
rules.why: The source loads the embedded blocklist once on first use into a frozen set for efficient repeated lookups.
rules.check: Flag embedded resource lookups that re-read or re-parse the resource per call or store it in a mutable collection.
